attempted_claim: Fix q in (0,1) and the Dabrowski-Landi-Sitarz-van Suijlekom-Varilly equivariant spectral triple (A=C(SU_q(2)), H, D_q) over quantum SU(2), with Peter-Weyl decomposition H = direct sum over spins j in (1/2)N_0 of spin-j subspaces. Let d_q be the Connes spectral distance d_q(phi,psi)=sup{|phi(a)-psi(a)|: a in A^{smooth}, ||[D_q,a]||<=1} and let phi_j be the vector state of a normalized highest-weight unit vector in the spin-j subspace, with phi_0 the state of the trivial representation. Prove or disprove that sup_{j} d_q(phi_0,phi_j) < infinity. A complete answer proves a finite uniform upper bound over all j with an explicit bound, or exhibits a subsequence j_k to infinity with a rigorous lower bound d_q(phi_0,phi_{j_k}) to infinity.
claim_type: prove-or-disprove uniform bound vs diverging subsequence
decisive_failure: The investigation reconstructed the DLSvSV spinor representation and Dirac spectrum and probed low-degree observables numerically, but it did not establish Lip-ball boundedness modulo scalars (the compact-quantum-metric-space property) nor exhibit a diverging subsequence, so the uniform boundedness question remains fully open and no partial bound is claimed.
